jobs.title: Water Agency Environmental Specialist I - Environmental Compliance
jobs.description:
**Position Information**
------------------------


**Sonoma Water is seeing a passionate and driven Environmental Specialist I professional to join our team!**  

**Join us in protecting and enhancing Sonoma County’s natural resources through meaningful, impactful work.**  

  

The Sonoma Water Agency is seeking a qualified candidate to fill a Water Agency Environmental Specialist I position responsible for working on environmental compliance and permitting matters for Sonoma Water projects.


At Sonoma Water, Environmental Specialists are responsible for evaluating, analyzing, and reporting on the environmental impacts of water supply, flood control, sanitation, and sustainability projects. To comply with federal, state, and local regulations, these positions assist in developing and proposing mitigation strategies to avoid, reduce, or offset the environmental impacts of projects. The Environmental Specialist I also uses an interdisciplinary approach from applied knowledge of biology, ecology, environmental science, and hydrology to:  

  

  

* Assist with the preparation of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) studies, such as categorical exemptions, mitigated negative declarations, environmental impact reports, and technical resource reports
* Assist with preparation of environmental regulatory permit applications to local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Perform field assessments and surveys for sensitive resources, such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife, botanical, and fisheries resources to evaluate environmental effects and determine potential impacts from projects
* Review natural resource studies and reports to understand historical and current site conditions of a project
* Review project information, schedules, studies, and designs, and assist in preparing tracking tools, standard operating procedures, and reports for projects
* Assist in the preparation and review of documents to comply with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right\-of\-way activities
* Stay up to date with environmental laws such as the CEQA, National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), Clean Water Act, Porter\-Cologne Water Quality Control Act, California and Federal Endangered Species Acts

  

The ideal candidate for this position is a team player and passionate about the environment and its resources. They will possess strong communication, problem\-solving, and project organizational skills. In addition, they will possess experience conducting many of the following activities:
* Knowledge of and experience with handling threatened, endangered, and/or sensitive species listed under state or federal endangered species acts (such as California red\-legged frog, California tiger salamander, steelhead trout, and California freshwater shrimp)
* Conducting field assessments and investigations for natural resources such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife and botanical resources in remote areas (e.g. agricultural lands, meadowlands, forests, and aquatic and riparian habitats)
* Collecting, analyzing, and reporting on environmental scientific data associated with natural resources, specifically wildlife
* Researching the historical land uses, existing conditions, and natural resources of a project site, and associated local, state, and federal regulations applicable to the resources and project
* Preparation of CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for public projects
* Applying for and acquiring environmental regulatory permits from local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Reviewing the development of public projects (specifically water utility projects) and their associated schedules, studies, and designs
* Collaborating with planners, engineers, contractors, and consultants on the design and construction of public projects (specifically water utility projects)

**Note: This position typically works Monday\-Friday during regular business hours but may be required to work evening, weekend, or holiday shifts to conduct field investigations, help with biological seasonal monitoring, and attend public meetings or community events.**

  

  

**About Sonoma Water**
  

Sonoma Water is a special district formed by the California State Legislature in 1949 and is responsible for providing a safe and reliable water supply to its customers in Sonoma and Marin counties. Sonoma Water also maintains 75 miles of flood control channels and provides sanitation services. Employing approximately 250 employees, Sonoma Water consists of four divisions, including Engineering \& Resource Planning, Environmental Resources, Business Services \& External Affairs, and Water/Wastewater Operations \& Maintenance. Sonoma Water supports the concept of environmental sustainability, focusing on renewable power sources, and strives to be a leader in its water use efficiency and fishery restoration programs.
  

  

Employees of Sonoma Water are employees of a special district and are not subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance of the County of Sonoma.**What We Offer**


Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits\* including:


* **Hybrid Telework** \- A schedule that meets the needs of our staff, department operations, and the communities we serve may be available depending on the assignment
* **Salary Advancement** \- A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full\-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
* **Paid Time Off** \- Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays

### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you looking to be part of a dynamic team who support sport fish conservation? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife’s Bay Delta Region\-Hatchery Operations and Interpretive Services Unit serves the public by enhancing recreational angling opportunities, managing sport fish populations, and providing outreach and educational programs that strengthen stewardship across the region.The Hatchery Operations and Interpretive Services Unit is seeking a motivated individual to work as a Environmental Scientist located in beautiful Sonoma County in Santa Rosa, California. You will play a key role implementing a Hatchery Genetic Management Plan (HGMP), as well as providing critical scientific and technical support for our hatchery operations.  

  

  

Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), this position supports the California Department of Fish and Wildlife’s Bay Delta Region hatchery operations by helping ensure Warm Springs Hatchery and Coyote Valley Fish Facility meet production, genetic management, and Endangered Species Act requirements for the Russian River steelhead program. The role analyzes biological and operational data, manages AquaManager databases, assists with NPDES water\-quality compliance, and supports aquatic invasive species monitoring. It also contributes to the Sport Fish Restoration Program by coordinating regional fish stocking, conducting fisheries and habitat assessments, developing management plans, and overseeing freshwater fishing contest permits and sport\-fish regulation recommendations.
  

  

Additionally, the position leads outreach and stakeholder engagement, evaluates regulation effectiveness, and provides technical expertise to Tribes, agencies, NGOs, and the public on warmwater and coldwater fisheries management.  

  

  

Be essential at the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW), where employees are valued and come together to manage and protect California’s diverse fish, wildlife, and habitats, for their ecological values and public enjoyment!

At Colliers it’s not our success that sets us apart, it’s how we achieve it. Our people are passionate, take ownership and always do what’s right for our clients, people and communities.


**Why Colliers?**

Our enterprising environment needs your expertise to facilitate Colliers’ continued growth as an industry leader. Our nimble, decentralized culture can provide you with a wealth of opportunities to learn about our business and quickly gain experience to accelerate your career.  



  

***\*\*\*This position is for a Sustainability Analyst in Sacramento, California \*\*\*\****

  

**About This Role**
-------------------

As part of the **REMS** team at Lincoln Plaza , the Sustainability Analyst will work with the Senior Project Manager on sustainability initiatives, environmental data tracking and reporting, management of service contracts related to environmental services and consultants, and collaboration with the Client's Sustainability team.  



  

* You will work directly with the Client, consultants, contractors, and internal staff to develop workflows for the LEED recertification process, including planning meetings, data collection and entry, tracking, and documentation. You will successfully track market activity using internal and external resources and provide company and industry research using online and in\-house resources.
* You will stay current on trends in sustainability, conservation, and green building operations. You will effectively collect, input, and track energy and water consumption data through EPA's ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and provide reports as requested. You will also track and report on federal, state, and local sustainability performance mandates.
You will successfully manage the existing LEED certification program for two (2\) Class A and one (1\) Class B office buildings. You will thrive in a fast\-paced environment where you can use your exceptional multitasking skills to meet tight deadlines while maintaining the highest standards of ethics and integrity.  
* 

  

**Essential Functions and Job Duties**
--------------------------------------

* Collect, analyze, and report sustainability performance data for buildings and operations.
* Manage and support reporting activities with The Climate Registry and other environmental reporting platforms.
* Coordinate and support LEED certification and recertification efforts across multiple facilities.
* Assist with WELL Building Standard and WELL Health\-Safety Rating initiatives.
* Monitor and track ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager performance metrics and benchmarking activities.
* Conduct sustainability assessments and identify opportunities for energy, water, waste, and carbon reduction, including quarterly water testing, indoor air quality (IAQ) testing, greenhouse gas inventories, and compliance with state mandates, executive orders, and Senate bills.
* Support environmental compliance programs and sustainability initiatives.
* Research and evaluate emerging sustainability trends, technologies, and best practices.
* Prepare presentations, reports, dashboards, and executive summaries for leadership and stakeholders.
* Collaborate with facility managers, consultants, contractors, and project teams to implement sustainability goals.
* Maintain documentation and records related to environmental programs, certifications, and sustainability reporting requirements.
Support organizational ESG and sustainability objectives through data analysis and performance measurement.  
* 

  

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

* At least two (2\) years of experience in environmental science, research, market analysis, or a related role within commercial real estate. A bachelor's degree in Environmental Science or a related field (Business, Economics, Statistics, etc.) is required.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
* Strong analytical skills and experience using various data sources and reporting platforms.
* LEED Green Associate (GA), LEED Accredited Professional (AP), ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, or CRIS experience is considered an asset.
Minimum of two (2\) years of professional experience in sustainability, environmental management, green building, energy management, or a related field.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

* LEED Green Associate (LEED GA), or
LEED Accredited Professional (LEED AP)

**Required Knowledge and Demonstrated Experience with the Following**

* The Climate Registry
* U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) programs
* LEED building certifications
* WELL Health\-Safety Rating
* WELL Building Standard
* ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager
* Green building and sustainability practices
* Environmental performance reporting and benchmarking
Sustainability metrics and data analysis

**Technical Skills**
--------------------

* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including: Excel (advanced formulas, pivot tables, data analysis, dashboards) Word PowerPoint Outlook
* Ability to analyze large datasets and develop meaningful reports and recommendations.
Experience with sustainability tracking and reporting tools is preferred.  
* 

  

**Communication Skills**
------------------------

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to effectively communicate technical sustainability information to diverse audiences.
* Strong presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.
Ability to prepare professional reports, executive summaries, and recommendations.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience supporting sustainability programs for commercial real estate, facilities

jobs.description:
**About FACS**


At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.

**Our Values**


We live our mission through three core values:

* **People First:** Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
* **Integrity of the Science:** Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence\-based practices.
* **Client Relationships for Life:** Build long\-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

**Why Join Us**

* **Impact:** Contribute meaningful work that empowers teams and drives results across the organization.
* **Culture:** Thrive in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission\-driven environment where your work matters.
* **Growth:** Innovate, develop your skills, and help shape the future of how we operate and deliver on our mission.
* **Visibility:** Partner directly with leadership and cross\-functional teams to make a real difference.


Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications—so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.

*Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at* FACS Experts.


**About the Role:**


The Environmental Health Specialist will support public health and well\-being by conducting fieldwork and environmental assessments for a variety of environmental health and industrial hygiene projects. Under the direction of Project Managers, you will support projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.


This is a field\-based role that requires regular travel to local client sites and occasional travel outside the local area, depending on project needs. You will collect samples and field data, document site conditions, prepare accurate field notes, and communicate project updates to Project Managers.


This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys hands\-on work, takes pride in accuracy and professionalism, and is eager to develop technical experience in environmental health and industrial hygiene. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong attention to detail, reliability, a positive work ethic, and a willingness to learn beyond their current comfort zone.

**Responsibilities:**

* Perform assigned fieldwork and project tasks under the direction of Project Managers.
* Travel regularly to local client sites and occasionally to out\-of\-area locations based on project needs.
* Support environmental health and industrial hygiene projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.
* Review project scopes, site requirements, and field protocols to ensure a clear understanding of assigned work.
* Collect field data and samples in accordance with established procedures, project specifications, and safety requirements.
* Conduct site observations and document field conditions accurately and thoroughly.
* Prepare, organize, maintain, and transport the tools, equipment, and supplies needed for assigned fieldwork.
* Maintain detailed field notes; compile data; and summarize findings to support project reporting and analysis.
* Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding project status, technical questions, field conditions, and next steps.
* Report progress, concerns, and deviations from project scope or established protocols promptly.
* Interact professionally and collaboratively with clients, contractors, building occupants, and other stakeholders at project sites.
* Follow all company safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
* Participate actively in training, mentorship, and professional\-development opportunities to build technical knowledge in environmental health and industrial hygiene.
* Support the delivery of high\-quality, timely client service while maintaining FACS’s standards for accuracy, professionalism, and integrity.

**What You Bring:**

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Reliable, professional, and able to follow field protocols, safety requirements, and project instructions.
* Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, current auto insurance, and a driving record that meets company standards.
* Ability to travel regularly to local client sites, with occasional out\-of\-area travel as needed.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of this field\-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on project requirements.

**Preferred**

* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Fieldwork or related experience in environmental services, construction, facilities, EHS, restoration, inspection, sampling, or technical documentation.
* Familiarity with asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, or air and exposure sampling

**Physical \& Work Requirements**

* Ability to perform field\-based work at client sites, including stooping, kneeling, climbing, crawling, and accessing a variety of areas to collect samples.
* Ability to lift, carry, and move equipment and instruments weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment and complete job\-related medical surveillance and respirator fit testing, as required for assigned work and consistent with applicable law.
* Ability to work at a desk and use a computer for extended periods to complete documentation and reporting.

jobs.description:
**Your new role:**  

To provide clinical care under supervision and acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to practice as a subspecialist Clinical Toxicologist
  
  

**About you:**  

**Fellowship activities:**  

The above goals are accomplished by a fellowship experience organized around the following areas of clinical training, research training and teaching opportunities:
  
  

Clinical Training
  
  

The fellow will work under the direct supervision of A/Prof Katherine Isoardi and other consultant clinical toxicologists in the clinical toxicology unit.
  
  

Attend daily clinical toxicology ward rounds at Princess Alexandra Hospital
  
Perform daily virtual ward rounds across Metro South HHS
  
Assess new poisoned patients that present through the PAH Emergency Department.
  
Provide phone consultation to peripheral hospitals calling for toxicology advice
  
Follow\-up Queensland cases referred to clinical toxicologists through the Poisons Centre
  
  

Research
  
  

Participation in recruitment, consent and data collection for research projects currently in operation.
  
Lead an observation research project in a poisoning chosen by the fellow with the assistance and supervision of A/Prof Isoardi. The fellow will be expected to present his/her findings at an academic meeting.
  
  

Check out our quick tips and application essentials!
  
  

**What we can offer you:**  

We offer a family\-friendly work environment that supports you in making the most of Queensland's laid\-back lifestyle.
  
We are renowned for teaching and research excellence with strong relations with Queensland's leading tertiary institutions.
  
We want to empower you to build a long\-term career, with countless opportunities to learn and grow, no matter your role
  
You'll have all the benefits of working for Queensland's world\-class public health system including generous leave entitlements, attractive salary and remuneration packages, salary packaging and access to relevant professional development allowances and/or leave, study and research assistance, corporate discounts and employee wellness programs.
  
  

**About us:**  

**Princess Alexandra Hospital:**  

The Princess Alexandra Hospital (PAH) is a tertiary health care centre providing care in most major adult specialties. We provide world class health care to Brisbane City's southern suburbs across emergency, medical, mental health and surgical services, including liver and kidney transplant.
  
  

We are nationally recognised for our expertise in trauma management and organ transplants and are one of Australia's leading academic and research health centres. The PAH as a major medical research precinct hosts Australia's most advanced medical research facility, the Translational Research Institute (TRI) as well as a new Clinical Research Facility for the discoveries made at TRI to be trialed in a safe clinical environment.
  
  

We're expanding our hospital to make sure everyone gets the care they need. We're adding more beds, modernising our buildings, and improving our spaces to treat kidney and cancer patients with all new services and facilities planned to open by 2027\.

Diversity of ideas, skills, traditions, and customs is celebrated as one of our greatest strengths. Having a workforce that reflects and understands the needs and expectations of our community is important to delivering safe, kinder, and more inclusive care.

* **Paid Time Off** \- Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays

new_jobs.title: Fellow in Clinical Toxicology
new_jobs.description:
**Your new role:**  

To provide clinical care under supervision and acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to practice as a subspecialist Clinical Toxicologist
  
  

**About you:**  

**Fellowship activities:**  

The above goals are accomplished by a fellowship experience organized around the following areas of clinical training, research training and teaching opportunities:
  
  

Clinical Training
  
  

The fellow will work under the direct supervision of A/Prof Katherine Isoardi and other consultant clinical toxicologists in the clinical toxicology unit.
  
  

Attend daily clinical toxicology ward rounds at Princess Alexandra Hospital
  
Perform daily virtual ward rounds across Metro South HHS
  
Assess new poisoned patients that present through the PAH Emergency Department.
  
Provide phone consultation to peripheral hospitals calling for toxicology advice
  
Follow\-up Queensland cases referred to clinical toxicologists through the Poisons Centre
  
  

Research
  
  

Participation in recruitment, consent and data collection for research projects currently in operation.
  
Lead an observation research project in a poisoning chosen by the fellow with the assistance and supervision of A/Prof Isoardi. The fellow will be expected to present his/her findings at an academic meeting.
  
  

Check out our quick tips and application essentials!
  
  

**What we can offer you:**  

We offer a family\-friendly work environment that supports you in making the most of Queensland's laid\-back lifestyle.
  
We are renowned for teaching and research excellence with strong relations with Queensland's leading tertiary institutions.
  
We want to empower you to build a long\-term career, with countless opportunities to learn and grow, no matter your role
  
You'll have all the benefits of working for Queensland's world\-class public health system including generous leave entitlements, attractive salary and remuneration packages, salary packaging and access to relevant professional development allowances and/or leave, study and research assistance, corporate discounts and employee wellness programs.
  
  

**About us:**  

**Princess Alexandra Hospital:**  

The Princess Alexandra Hospital (PAH) is a tertiary health care centre providing care in most major adult specialties. We provide world class health care to Brisbane City's southern suburbs across emergency, medical, mental health and surgical services, including liver and kidney transplant.
  
  

We are nationally recognised for our expertise in trauma management and organ transplants and are one of Australia's leading academic and research health centres. The PAH as a major medical research precinct hosts Australia's most advanced medical research facility, the Translational Research Institute (TRI) as well as a new Clinical Research Facility for the discoveries made at TRI to be trialed in a safe clinical environment.
  
  

We're expanding our hospital to make sure everyone gets the care they need. We're adding more beds, modernising our buildings, and improving our spaces to treat kidney and cancer patients with all new services and facilities planned to open by 2027\.
  
  

INTEGRITY \| COMPASSION \| ACCOUNTABILITY \| RESPECT \| ENGAGEMENT \| EXCELLENCE
  
  

Our values were created by employees for employees to shape our culture and inspire positive interactions in the workplace. Diversity of ideas, skills, traditions, and customs is celebrated as one of our greatest strengths. Having a workforce that reflects and understands the needs and expectations of our community is important to delivering safe, kinder, and more inclusive care.
  
  

We recognise our strength comes from the diversity of our people and so we encourage people of all genders, ethnicities, ages, abilities, languages, sexual orientation, and family responsibilities to apply.
